reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent static review against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP (retail PE view_1), radare2 6.2.0 CFG and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe; candidate source read from this worktree. No game process was executed and no runtime behavior is claimed.
review_basis: Retail 0x00407E30 was re-disassembled, re-decompiled and re-CFG'd through the live Binary Ninja view, independently recovered with radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast. The candidate is scripts/GameNatives/defineq/00407E30-DefineQMaterial.cpp at sha256 445f304451962003a56a3136bdce597b5e5a0b365515c51c70890b86f77ab421 (recorded implementation.signature: int32_t DefineQMaterial(long param_1, long param_2, long param_3, int32_t param_4, int32_t param_5);). The evidence artifact digests are bound in this review.

checks.name: abi_and_signature
checks.detail: BN (long double arg1 @ st0, long double arg2 @ st1, long double arg3 @ st2, int32_t arg4, int32_t arg5 @ 0xc): three x87 register inputs, the result buffer at [E+4], and the frame at [E+0xc]. The candidate (long double context, long double arg2, long double arg3, int arg4, int arg5) puts all three long doubles on the stack, which shifts arg4/arg5 by 36 bytes and reads neither the x87 inputs nor the right frame slot.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports "int32_t(long double arg1 @ st0, long double arg2 @ st1, long double arg3 @ st2, int32_t arg4, int32_t arg5 @ 0xc)" at 0x00407E30; radare2 recovers "fcn.00407e30 (int32_t arg_24h, int32_t arg_28h);". Both tools place the entry at 0x00407E30 and agree on the stack/register word count and cleanup; the difference is the level of type/argument-name detail, not the call frame. Candidate declaration: int32_t DefineQMaterial(long param_1, long param_2, long param_3, int32_t param_4, int32_t param_5);. The candidate declaration is separately recorded as divergent below and does not satisfy the retail ABI.
